properties.description:
We are attempting to rectify a situation where a permitted building straddles two property lines of properties owned by two different entities, one being us. We think we desire an LBA to run west to east across parcel 232403-9005 at the meeting point of 257016-0000 and 232403-9164. This would enlarge 0000 to encompass the northern portion of 9005 and the entire carport which straddles both parcels.We would need to contact the condominium owners' board at 0000 to settle on terms of the property exchange before executing the LBA. 
We prefer to keep the remaining portion of 9005 as a separate parcel and as a greenbelt. We would be happy to sell the greenbelt (9005) to the City as a permanent open green space if that is of interest. Otherwise, we could attach the remainder of 9005 to one of our properties along the alley easement (5007 and 5013 38th Ave SW, parcel numbers 232403-9148 and 232403-9149). This is only an option for us if we can receive ironclad assurances in writing from the City and King County that the yearly property taxes on the 9005 square footage could never leap. Currently, 9005 is taxed at a $1000. rate for land value on 5750 SF. Our 5007 38th SW property (9148) is $731,200. land value for 5850SF (as is 9149).
Any thoughts, suggestions, and advice very much appreciated. 
Thank you!

properties.description: Hello SDCI - hope you are doing well. We are planning to build a 560sf DADU, 315sf home addition and 390sf garage on our property in North Seattle. Please see included Preliminary Site Plan. We also plan to demolish an existing overhead carport and vault a couple interior ceilings - all under 14-feet in span. I am a registered Architect in Seattle, but mainly work on larger commercial projects so this is some new territory for me. Would LOVE to be able to come in to the office and get some over-the-counter assistance, but hoping that this at least get the conversation going about our project. A few things have come up that I need some help on. One of the main ones is this pesky dashed Lot Line drawn on the Assessors map, shown 10-feet south of the northern Property Line. I can't see any use for this and am hoping we can dimension our side yard set back from our Property Line and not this Lot Line - just submitted a Land Use Analysis question via the portal regarding this. Another is regarding STFI permits and if we should submit all but the DADU as an STFI or all of the work under a single building permit. Assuming submitting as much as possible as an STFI is cheaper?
